day: # The lectionary of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church (variant malankara),
# as St. George Indian Orthodox Church, Melbourne, keeps it in its Lectionary
# Each Sunday and feast has its Gospel at Vespers (Ramsho, the evening before
# in the Church's reckoning, listed on the day) and at Matins (Sapro), the
# lessons before the Holy Qurbana (Old Testament, read as "ot") and the
# Qurbana's Acts or Catholic Epistle, Pauline Epistle and Gospel.  The
# weekdays of the Great Fast and the Fast of Nineveh have their morning
# lessons; Holy Week its Midnight Office and the hours.  The Sundays after
# Pentecost run to the Transfiguration, then the Sundays after it and after
# Shunoyo to the Cross.  The occasional services (sacraments, ordinations,
# burial) and the commons of saints have no date and are left out.  Printing
# errors corrected or left out are in docs/source-errors.csv.

day: # The lectionary of the Syriac Orthodox Church of Antioch (variant syriac), from
# Scripture Readings: Qeryone men kthobo qadisho (Archdiocese of the Syriac
# Orthodox Church in the Eastern USA, New Jersey edition, 2000), a table per
# day giving book and chapter and verse in English, Arabic and Syriac.  The
# book does not say at which service each reading is read: the Old Testament
# lessons, the Acts or Catholic Epistle and the Pauline Epistle come first and
# the Gospels (usually three, of Vespers, Matins and the Qurbana) after, in
# the book's order.  Holy Week has its services and hours, Pentecost the
# three parts of the Kneeling Service.  The book numbers the Sundays from
# Easter (New Sunday the first, Pentecost the seventh) to the 24th; any left
# when the Cross comes give way to the Sundays after it.  The book puts St Stephen
# after John the Baptist (7 January), so on 8 January.  The commons of saints,
# the occasional services and the unassigned weekday readings are left out.
# Printing errors corrected or left out are in docs/source-errors.csv.
